issue.title: Update My Work Tab with Stage Accordions and Observer Chapters
issue.body: My Work displays a flat list of chapters actively assigned to the current user, which serves a translator with a handful of assigned chapters but leaves Observers with nothing: Observers are never assigned work, so no chapter reaches their list and there is no entry point into one. This ticket does two things to the same screen. It groups My Work into one collapsible accordion per workflow stage, so a list spanning several stages stays scannable. And it extends the list's population rule so that chapters a user holds the Observer role over, and Peer Check chapters with no assigned Peer Checker, appear alongside the chapters assigned to them as a translator. The two changes belong together because either one alone leaves the tab in a half-converted state. The read-only draft surface an Observer lands on is built in #452, and the download the chip triggers is built in #508. ## Functional Requirements ### List Population Show a chapter from any project the user belongs to when one of the following is true: - The chapter is in Drafting or Peer Check and is assigned to the user (unchanged from today). - The chapter is in Peer Check with no assigned Peer Checker, the user is a translator on the project, and the user did not draft it. - The chapter is in Community Review, Linguist Check, Theologian Check, or Consultant Check and the user holds the Observer role on the project; no assignment is needed. Keep a chapter in the list until its stage advances to Complete. ### Stage Accordions - Group the list into one collapsible accordion per workflow stage, collapsed by default, for every user, not only Observers, so a translator's existing flat list becomes grouped by stage as well. - Show the stage's status icon to the left of the stage name in each accordion header, using the same icon set as the workflow status badge on today's chapter row. - Show the chapter count in each accordion header (e.g. "Community Review (12)"). - Render an accordion only for a stage where the user has at least one chapter; do not show empty accordions. - Expand the accordion automatically when it is the only one present, so a user with work in a single stage sees their chapters without tapping. - Order the accordions by workflow order: Drafting, Peer Check, Community Review, Linguist Check, Theologian Check, Consultant Check. - Order chapters within an accordion most-recently-entered-that-stage first. ### Chapter Rows - Keep every element of the existing chapter row except the workflow status badge, which moves to the accordion header: the phase status icon, book and chapter name, sync state indicator, last activity date, and the `li:chevron-right` drilldown arrow. - Show a right-aligned, icon-only download chip (no text label) on an assigned chapter whose Tier 1 content is missing, using the muted gray outline treatment and `li:cloud-off` icon from the existing "Source not downloaded" chip. - Show the same icon-only chip on an Observer chapter whose draft audio is not on the device; trigger, tap behavior, and download progress for this chip are specified in #508. - Show the same icon-only chip on a Peer Check chapter, assigned or open, whose draft audio is not on the device; trigger, tap behavior, and download progress for this chip are specified in #704. - Right-align every row's chip to the same column, so chips line up vertically down the list regardless of row content length. - Tapping a row opens the chapter in the drafting/checking flow for an assigned chapter, and in the read-only draft view for an Observer chapter. ### Empty State - Show an empty state when the user has no chapters in any stage. ### Navigation - Let an Observer browse their projects through the existing Milestones tab; My Work is the fast path to a chapter, not the only path. - Do not build a new project-level or book-level navigation screen for Observers. - Do not show stage-advancement controls on any row; the project manager or translator advances every stage. > **Note:** Collapsed stage accordions are what make an Observer's list usable, and they replace an earlier plan to scope each Observer to particular stages on the backend. A community member doing Community Review and a theologian doing a Theologian Check are the same role with the same permissions, so the list is populated identically for both and each opens the section they care about. This keeps the change client-side: no stage-scope field on the project association, no web UI to set it, and no cross-platform dependency. > **Note:** Open question, unresolved at ticket creation. If Community Review advances per pericope rather than per chapter, rows need to name the portion rather than the whole chapter, and the list's unit of work changes with it. Confirm before building the row label.
